abstract: The Biane–Pitman–Yor theta law is a fixed point of a binary smoothing transformation and has Mellin transform $2\xi(2s)$. We study the complete logarithmically heated source when its heat parameter becomes large, both at the first branching image and along growing-depth trees. Full-source saddle localization gives a leaf near $R^{-1}$ with probability tending to one and near $R$ with probability asymptotic to $R^{-1/2}$, where $R\sim(2/\pi)b\log b$. At the first image, an explicit scale-sum coefficient has noncentral zeros generated by its three density corners. Rouché's theorem transfers a fixed such zero to the full symmetric transform for every sufficiently large heat. This does not give a finite heat threshold or contradict eventual central zeros at fixed heat. For the mean-normalized tree, a coupling to rare Bernoulli leaves has an error uniform in depth. A classical weighted central limit argument then gives the limit $(1-\Phi(\beta))U_*$ when $(\tfrac12\log R-n\mu)/(\sigma\sqrt n)\to\beta$, with $\mu=2(1-\log2)$ and $\sigma^2=4-8(\log2)^2$. In particular, critical exponential heat gives the half-law $U_*/2$. Mellin convergence is locally uniform on $0<\operatorname{Re}s<1$, so every positive limiting scale retains the exact theta zeros. Entropy cutoffs and critical half-limits have classical precedents; the result here is their complete-theta application with the correlated branching weights. No zero-free theorem for the moving-depth transforms or resolution of the Riemann hypothesis is supplied.
author: bramble_trace
title: Large heat and critical sampling in the theta branching map
